title: Defining Web Users
breadcrumbs: Inbound and Inventory Trading Partner Management

children:
Before customers can access their order information through Trading 
 Partner Management, you must first configure them as a web user. The system 
 supports two types of users: external 
 and    internal:

: 
 Has access to certain company(s) 
 information. An external user is not employed by your organization. You 
 can restrict an external user's access to one customer (via a customer 
 ID) or a series of customers (via the customer group value). Common external 
 users include customers, business partners and suppliers. These people 
 need access only to their own shipments. You will need to associate an 
 external user to either a customer ID or a customer group value to view 
 shipment information.

: 
 Has a greater freedom of access, based on how you define his/her web user 
 profile. An internal user who is employed by your organization. You can 
 use the Assigned Companies Tab and Assigned Customer ID Tab to limit the 
 internal user's access; if you don't use these tabs to set limits, external 
 users have access to all shipments in the system. These people can use 
 Trading Partner Management to access any shipment in the system.
Ship To Selection Access Tab Fields

Use the Web User 
 Field to identify the user name. He/she will use this name to logon 
 to the Trading Partner Management website.

Use the Email Address Field 
 to enter the user's email address (for example,   customer@store.com). This field supports up to 500 characters. It is mandatory, else a validation message will be displayed. Also, duplicate email addresses in the web user configuration records are not allowed.

Use the User 
 Type Field to indicate the type of web user you are defining (external 
 or internal).

Use the Order 
 Processing Field to indicate how you want the system to handle 
 orders that are entered via Trading Partner Management.

- Automatic: If you choose 
 this method, the system will automatically create the orders for this 
 user through Trading Partner Management. No additional user intervention 
 is required.

Use this tab to identify which companies this user can access shipments 
 for. The fields displayed on this tab will depend on whether you chose 
 to create an external or internal user. Generally, external users should 
 be associated with only one company; internal users are typically associated 
 with multiple companies.

If this is an external user, 
 you will need to assign him/her a customer ID, a customer group, and/or 
 a vendor. This is required for external users to view their own order 
 information. If this is a multi-company environment, the customer ID, 
 along with the company, determines what orders this user can access.

If this is an 
 internal user, associate him/her with a company   if 
 you want to limit access to only order information for customers of that 
 company. Internal users will have access to all the customers of whichever 
 company(s) 
 they are authorized to view.

Using the Ship to Selection 
 Access Tab

Use this tab to identify which order ship to selection 
 record that you want this user to have access to when entering web orders. 
 These records contain the rules for selecting a series of ship to addresses 
 for your order.

Using the Item Selection 
 Access Tab

Use this tab to identify which order item selection 
 record that you want this user to have access to when entering web orders. 
 These records contain the rules for selecting a series of item(s) for 
 your order.
